subject.title: fix(openai): allow RFC 2544 fake-IP range for Realtime session requests

question: Should OpenClaw accept this hostname-scoped fake-IP SSRF exception for OpenAI Realtime session-secret requests, and should the helper be exposed through the public Plugin SDK?
rationale: The implementation is narrow, but it intentionally moves a security boundary and expands public Plugin SDK surface, which requires maintainer intent rather than automated cleanup.

options.title: Accept After Rebase
options.body: Approve the scoped SSRF and SDK tradeoff, then require conflict resolution, refreshed SDK budgets, and focused API/test proof before merge.

options.title: Keep Policy Local
options.body: Use the same `SsrFPolicy` shape inside the OpenAI plugin and avoid exporting another public Plugin SDK helper.

options.title: Decline The Exception
options.body: Leave fake-IP proxy users on DNS/proxy exclusions or disabled fake-IP mode for Realtime until a broader networking policy is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept After Rebase
recommendation.body: Approve the scoped SSRF and SDK tradeoff, then require conflict resolution, refreshed SDK budgets, and focused API/test proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the fake-IP SSRF helper and appears in current history for the Realtime/SSRF surfaces this decision affects.
